scenarios.title: Early cross or take him on?
scenarios.setup: You are on the right wing with the ball. The full-back is a few steps away and has not closed you down. Your far-post runner is free; the striker is marked.

options.label: Whip an early cross to the free far-post runner
options.why: The full-back has not closed you down, so you have time to look up and deliver before the defence shifts to the far post.

options.label: Dribble at the full-back first
options.why: You can beat him, but it costs time and the box shifts to cover the far post.

options.label: Pass back to the midfielder
options.why: Safe, but it gives up a good chance while the far post is free.

options.label: Cross to the marked striker at the near post
options.why: He is tight to his marker, so it is easy to intercept.

scenarios.title: Come short or run in behind?
scenarios.setup: Your marker is tight on your back and the defence is playing a high line. Your midfielder has the ball and is looking up.

options.label: Check short to drag your marker out, then spin in behind
options.why: The first movement creates the space: the defender follows you out, and the ball goes into the gap he left.

options.label: Stand still and ask for the ball to feet
options.why: With a defender tight on your back you cannot turn, and the high line stays compact.

options.label: Sprint in behind right away
options.why: You start level with the line, so you risk being offside and the defender is not dragged anywhere.

options.label: Run sideways, away from the ball
options.why: It takes you out of the game and does not help your midfielder.

scenarios.title: Man on
scenarios.setup: You receive the ball in midfield and a defender is pressing hard right behind you. A teammate is free on your left, facing forward.

options.label: One touch to the free teammate on your left
options.why: With a defender on your back you play first time to the free player: you keep the ball and keep the move going.

options.label: Turn into the pressure
options.why: Turning with a defender right behind you risks losing it in a dangerous area.

options.label: Take a touch and shield the ball
options.why: Shielding buys a second, but the defender and a second presser close you down.

options.label: Hit a long ball over the top
options.why: A low-percentage ball: nobody is set to win it and it gives possession away.

scenarios.title: Jockey or tackle?
scenarios.setup: A winger is dribbling at you with the ball a stride ahead of him. Your centre-back is covering behind you.

options.label: Jockey, show him outside and wait for a bad touch
options.why: Stay on your feet, slow him down and force him wide: your cover is behind you, so there is no need to gamble.

options.label: Slide in now
options.why: If you miss, he is past you and the defence is broken.

options.label: Backpedal as fast as you can
options.why: It gives him all the space and the time to pick a pass.

options.label: Dive in and poke at the ball
options.why: Diving in lets him go past with one touch.

scenarios.title: The striker drops deep
scenarios.setup: Your marker drops into midfield, away from your line. Your holding midfielder is nearby and can see him.

options.label: Let him go, pass him on to your midfielder and keep the line
options.why: Do not follow him out of the back line: tell the midfielder to pick him up and keep the shape behind.

options.label: Follow him all the way into midfield
options.why: You leave a big gap behind you that a runner can attack.

options.label: Step up tight to win the ball
options.why: If he turns, you are out of position and beaten with the line broken.

options.label: Drop back into your own box
options.why: You give him all the time and space in front of goal.

scenarios.title: Shoot or square?
scenarios.setup: You are in on goal. The keeper has come out to close you down and a teammate is unmarked close to an empty goal.

options.label: Square it to your free teammate
options.why: The keeper has committed to you, so the pass leaves your teammate a tap-in at an open goal.

options.label: Shoot at the keeper
options.why: He has closed the angle, so you are likely to hit him.

options.label: Try to dribble round the keeper
options.why: It is a risk you do not need to take when a teammate is free.

options.label: Hold it and wait for the defence to arrive
options.why: Waiting gives a recovering defender time to close the pass down.

scenarios.title: Shoot from distance or pass?
scenarios.setup: Two defenders are closing you down. A teammate is unmarked in the box with a clear passing lane.

options.label: Pass to the unmarked teammate in the box
options.why: A clear lane to a free player in a better position beats a long shot through two defenders.

options.label: Shoot from here
options.why: The two defenders are in the way and the shot is a long one.

options.label: Dribble between the two defenders
options.why: You are likely to lose it in the most dangerous area of the pitch.

options.label: Play it back to the midfield
options.why: Safe, but you give up a clear chance.

scenarios.title: The 3v2 counter-attack
scenarios.setup: You break away in the middle with a runner on each side. Two defenders are back.

options.label: Carry the ball at the defenders until one commits, then pass to the free runner
options.why: Running at them fixes both defenders, and whoever steps to you leaves a runner free on the other side.

options.label: Pass wide the moment you get it
options.why: The defenders have time to slide across and cover.

options.label: Shoot from 30 metres
options.why: A low-percentage shot when you have two free runners.

options.label: Slow down and wait for support
options.why: The other defenders recover and the chance is gone.

scenarios.title: Switch the play
scenarios.setup: You are on the right with the ball and three opponents have shifted over. A teammate is free on the far side with plenty of space.

options.label: Switch it with a long diagonal to the free player on the far side
options.why: The opposition has shifted across, so the far side is open: one pass changes the whole picture.

options.label: Dribble into the crowd
options.why: Three defenders are waiting for you.

options.label: Play it short to the marked teammate
options.why: It keeps the ball on the crowded side, where the pressure is.

options.label: Play it long down the line
options.why: It gives the ball away and the team cannot get up in support.

scenarios.title: Where do you support?
scenarios.setup: Your teammate has the ball wide on the right with a defender in front of him. You want to give him an option.

options.label: Behind the ball and inside, at about 45 degrees, in a clear passing lane
options.why: A support angle gives a clear pass line and keeps the ball moving.

options.label: Level with the ball, in the same line
options.why: A pass can go through two of you at once, and a defender can mark both.

options.label: Stay where you are, far away
options.why: The ball carrier has no option and gets closed down.

options.label: Run in front of him down the line
options.why: He cannot pass it forward without the offside risk, and he gets squeezed.

scenarios.title: Near post or far post?
scenarios.setup: A cross is coming in from the right wing. The keeper is cheating towards the near post and the defenders are watching the ball.

options.label: Attack the far post, arriving late
options.why: The keeper and defenders are drawn to the near post, so the far post is where the space is.

options.label: Run to the near post
options.why: The keeper is already guarding it and the defenders are close.

options.label: Stay on the penalty spot
options.why: You are easy to mark and you wait for the ball to arrive.

options.label: Drop off to the edge of the box
options.why: You give up your best chance to score from the cross.

scenarios.title: The recovery run
scenarios.setup: The attacker has beaten your line and is running at goal. You are chasing back from behind.

options.label: Curve your run to the goal side, between the ball and goal
options.why: Getting goal side first stops the attacker running straight at goal.

options.label: Chase straight after the ball
options.why: You will not catch him and you stay behind the ball.

options.label: Stop and shout for help
options.why: You are out of the play and he runs through.

options.label: Slide in from behind
options.why: A tackle from behind is a foul and a card.

scenarios.title: Dummy or half turn?
scenarios.setup: A pass is coming to you. You scanned: there is space directly behind you and the nearest defender is far away.

options.label: Dummy it: let it roll past you and spin after it
options.why: Space behind you and no pressure: the dummy takes a defender out of the game and wins you time.

options.label: Take it with your back to goal and stand still
options.why: You waste the space behind you.

options.label: Play it first time back
options.why: Safe, but it throws away a chance to keep the attack moving.

options.label: Hit it long first time
options.why: You have not looked up, so it is a guess.

scenarios.title: Overlap or underlap?
scenarios.setup: Your winger has the ball facing his full-back. The inside lane is crowded with two defenders, the outside lane is free.

options.label: Overlap: run round the outside past your winger
options.why: The inside is crowded and the outside is empty: the overlap gives him an extra option and pulls the full-back out.

options.label: Underlap through the crowded inside lane
options.why: There are two defenders waiting there.

options.label: Stay behind the ball
options.why: Your winger is on his own against two players.

options.label: Run to the middle
options.why: You take yourself away from the winger and give him no option.

scenarios.title: Hold it up or turn?
scenarios.setup: You receive the ball with your back to goal and a centre-back tight behind you. A midfielder is arriving from deep.

options.label: Hold it up, shield it and lay it off to the arriving midfielder
options.why: With a defender tight on your back you cannot turn: shield it and play the runner coming onto it.

options.label: Turn quickly with him on your back
options.why: If you cannot see him, you will lose it.

options.label: Shoot with your back to goal
options.why: You cannot hit the target facing the wrong way.

options.label: Pass it back to the centre-back
options.why: It kills the attack: you give up the ball and the move.

scenarios.title: Play out or clear?
scenarios.setup: You are on the ball in your own box and the striker is pressing you. Your full-back is free and unmarked in the wide channel.

options.label: Play it to the free full-back
options.why: A free outlet beats a panic clearance: you keep possession and play away from the press.

options.label: Clear it as far as you can
options.why: It gives the ball away and the press starts again.

options.label: Dribble past the striker
options.why: A mistake in your own box leads to a goal.

options.label: Pass across your own box
options.why: It risks an interception right in front of goal.

scenarios.title: The 2v1
scenarios.setup: You and a teammate are attacking one defender near the box. He is between you and goal.

options.label: Run at the defender and pass when he commits
options.why: Attack him with the ball: when he steps to you the pass opens, and your teammate is free to finish.

options.label: Pass straight away from here
options.why: It lets the defender stay where he is and cover both of you.

options.label: Shoot from here
options.why: You are well out, and the defender is in the way.

options.label: Dribble round him alone
options.why: You are throwing away a free teammate.

scenarios.title: Force him wide
scenarios.setup: A winger comes at you in the middle of the pitch. You want to steer him away from the goal and onto his weaker foot.

options.label: Show him to the touchline, side-on, blocking the inside route
options.why: Force him wide and onto his weaker foot: the touchline is a defender too.

options.label: Stand square in front of him
options.why: He can go either way.

options.label: Back off towards your goal
options.why: You give him all the time and the space to run at the box.

options.label: Dive in with your foot out
options.why: You get dribbled past and the middle is open.

scenarios.title: Press or hold?
scenarios.setup: Their midfielder takes a heavy first touch away from his body, and you are close to the ball.

options.label: Press now: a heavy touch is a trigger
options.why: A bad touch is the best moment to press: you win it or force a mistake.

options.label: Hold your position and wait
options.why: The moment passes and he recovers the ball.

options.label: Drop back to your own half
options.why: You give up a great chance to win it high.

options.label: Slide in from far away
options.why: You will arrive late and miss.

scenarios.title: Carry it or pass it?
scenarios.setup: You have the ball in midfield. There is open space ahead and nobody is pressing you.

options.label: Drive forward with the ball into the space
options.why: Carrying it forward draws a defender towards you and opens a passing lane for a teammate.

options.label: Pass it back
options.why: There is no pressure, so there is no reason to give it up.

options.label: Hit a long ball immediately
options.why: You have time, so make a better choice.

options.label: Stand still and look for options
options.why: The opposition has time to recover and close the gaps.

scenarios.title: Cut it back
scenarios.setup: You have beaten your man to the goal line. The defenders are covering the near post, and a teammate is arriving at the penalty spot.

options.label: Cut it back along the ground to the penalty spot
options.why: It buys time for the runner and the defenders are moving against the ball.

options.label: Cross it high to the near post
options.why: The defenders are standing there, and a high ball goes straight to them.

options.label: Shoot from the tight angle
options.why: The angle is tight and the keeper has it covered.

options.label: Take another touch
options.why: You give a defender time to get back and block it.

scenarios.title: Time your run
scenarios.setup: A teammate is about to play a through ball. The last defender is level with you and the defensive line is high.

options.label: Hold your run, then go as the pass is played
options.why: Start from behind the line and go on the pass, so you stay onside.

options.label: Run now before the pass
options.why: You will be in an offside position when the ball is played.

options.label: Stand level and wait for the ball to arrive
options.why: The defence steps up and catches you offside.

options.label: Run towards the ball
options.why: You drag nobody out and you leave the space behind alone.
